A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DSP and retain the same central sequence-parallelism mechanism. All pages, figures, tables and equations were readable through extraction and visual inspection. V1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendix A.1–A.4.

before.justification: V1 Section 4.1 and Figure 3 report original throughput measurements comparing DSP with DeepSpeed-Ulysses on a 724M ST-DiT model.

after.justification: V2 Section 5 and Figures 5–9 report original performance, scaling, inference-latency and memory measurements, with experimental settings supplied in Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: Both versions use all-to-all resharding between computation stages so that attention can execute locally along the required dimension. V2 expands the description with Switch/Split/Gather primitives and an API, without establishing a different DSP algorithm. Removing cross-attention concerns the benchmark model.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate spatial-temporal, video-style transformer workloads; neither reports evaluation on a named dataset or another application domain. The OpenSora-like benchmark, larger configurations and additional timing measurements change settings and measurement procedures within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: V1 lists Megatron-SP in its setup and discusses Ring-Attention, but Figure 3 reports only DeepSpeed-Ulysses against DSP. V2 Figures 5–9 additionally report Megatron-SP, labeled Megatron-LM in the plots, and Ring-Attention, substantially broadening the empirical comparison.

E3.justification: V1 uses a 724M ST-DiT model with cross-attention on H800 GPUs, batch size one and 2–8 GPUs. V2 uses 720M and 3B cross-attention-free models on H100 GPUs. It adds minimum-feasible sequence parallelism combined with data parallelism on 128 GPUs, weak/strong scaling through 64 GPUs, TFLOPS/GPU reporting, and latency and memory measurements.

E4.justification: V1 Figure 3 already investigates throughput scaling. V2 substantially extends this with separate weak/strong scaling analyses, intra-node and inter-node comparisons, attention-head and memory scaling limits, and allocated-versus-cached memory analysis in Figures 6–9. These investigate practical scalability and memory overhead beyond the original throughput study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's black reference boxes indicate linear scaling, and its shaded memory bars distinguish cached memory; neither represents statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: The original Figure 3 results are replaced by substantially expanded results under different hardware, models and protocols. V1 reports 42.0%–216.8% throughput improvement over Ulysses; v2 Section 5.1 reports 32%–75% over Ulysses and up to 10x over other baselines. V2 also adds scaling-limit, inference-latency and memory findings. These are not same-setting performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: V2 adds an explicit communication-minimization problem constrained by GPU memory capacity in Equation 6 and formal sharding-state definitions in Table 2. Its communication analysis revises Ring-Attention from 4M in v1 Table 1 to 2M in v2 Table 3, explaining communication along the sharded temporal dimension. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central dynamic-switching contribution and claimed minimum 75% communication reduction remain. V2 revises the headline throughput range from 42.0%–216.8% to 32.2%–10x and makes the high-level API an explicit part of its usability contribution. Presenting DSP as an abstraction largely reframes the retained mechanism.

C2.justification: V1 Section 4.1 extrapolates its findings to language-model training without explicit applicability limitations. V2 Section 6 states that DSP may not suit single-dimensional language models and may lose efficiency on operations involving every sequence dimension. V2 also adds explanations for head-count-independent scaling and superlinear scaling through reduced optimizer and gradient overhead.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents benchmark simplification, layers, hidden sizes, attention heads, patch sizes, baseline implementation sources, ZeRO-2 usage, parallel-group settings, resolution processing and four API functions. This substantially expands the sparse implementation information in v1. Both versions retain the same OpenDiT code address; this is not a newly announced code release.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including GQA, FlashAttention, Mamba, RWKV, OpenSora and FSDP, while removing Longformer, LongRoPE and Llama. It expands discussion of attention-head limits and Ring-Attention communication costs. The principal positioning against existing single-sequence parallelism methods remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and background are extensively rewritten. V2 reorganizes DSP into overview, problem definition, primitives and adaptability subsections, separates theoretical analysis, expands the experimental narrative, and adds discussion and an implementation appendix. These substantially change the exposition and structure beyond adding results.

P2.justification: V2 adds conceptual and system diagrams, expanded performance/scaling plots, latency and memory displays, settings tables and an API example. The original Figure 1 is retained as appendix Figure 10, while Figure 2 is redrawn as Figure 4. New plots introduce additional comparator series, different axes, failure markers and scaling references.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens v1's sparse empirical support through additional measured competitors, two model sizes, scaling, latency and memory evidence, while providing implementation details and concrete applicability limits. These improve the paper's assessability and support for its systems claims. Tradeoffs remain: the benchmark omits cross-attention, and Table 3 implies only a 50% communication reduction versus Ring-Attention at two GPUs, conflicting with the retained 75% minimum claim. These issues temper but do not outweigh the substantial gains.
